quest.title: Joy Above the Clouds
quest.description: Your friends have promised to provide clues and new ideas to solve the riddle. You expectantly wait at the agreed upon time, planning to convene and go over all you have learned with Sucrose...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Lazurite Swirl x1, Mora x20000, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, great timing! We got a lot of letters in the mailbox, and I just finished sorting them into four groups!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice work!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Well, the real work hasn't even started yet... Which batch of letters should we read through first?

talks.objective: Go to the alchemy crafting bench and meet up with Sucrose
Take a look at the Clue Board and read the letters

choices.text: Read Letters About "A Flower That Is Not of This World"

response.speaker: Clue Board
response.text: About the "flower that is not of this world"...

choices.text: Read Letters About "A Flower That Is Not of This World"
Read Letters About "A Guide Who Will Never Get Lost"

response.speaker: Clue Board
response.text: About the "guide who will never get lost"...

choices.text: Read Letters About "One Who Would Never Lie"

response.speaker: Clue Board
response.text: About the "one who would never lie"...

choices.text: Read Letters About "A Legend That Never Ends"

response.speaker: Clue Board

choices.text: Read Letters About "A Guide Who Will Never Get Lost"
Read Letters About "One Who Would Never Lie"
Read Letters About "A Legend That Never Ends"

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Let me quickly summarize what we've found out about "a flower that is not of this world."

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Tighnari believes that on closer examination, it might be logically paradoxical, while Albedo says that his answer would be better discussed at length in person...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: As for my answer... I think a clock in the shape of a flower would constitute one "that is not of this world."

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Here's what we've gathered regarding "a guide who will never get lost."

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #Mona said that she'd like to join us in uncovering the secret behind the prophecy, while Bennett suggests Fischl, Mona, or {NICKNAME} as potential candidates.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Mika didn't submit much, but he did draw a vegetation map for Master Tighnari and wrote up a dragon-spotting calendar for Cyno...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Amber also wrote in... She said that she sees herself as nobody's guide, but everybody's friend.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: As for "one who would never lie"... Rosaria removed herself from consideration, but both Razor and Cyno are willing to support us in our search.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Timaeus seems to have forgotten to write to us...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: And finally, this is what we've gathered on "a legend that never ends." Klee said that her mom has a number of friends who like to write storybooks...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Lisa believes that legends live forever in people's hearts. I think that for a legend to be never-ending, it has to be filled with hopes and dreams, and actively passed from one person to the next.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... what're the answers to the four riddles then?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Uhh... you're really smart, Paimon! I bet you can figure it all out in no time!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Or... let's all share our thoughts on what we think the answers might be.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Wait! *panting* ...Wait for me!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Oh, Timaeus! What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I really am... the time just got away from me, and I didn't get around to writing that letter. However! I'm happy to announce that I think I can be the "one who would never lie"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? This is kinda sudden!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not that we don't trust you, Timaeus, but um... Could you elaborate a little? After you catch your breath...?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Of course, of course... Phew.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Do you still remember the time I, uh, ahem, collaborated with a certain Miss Ying'er?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Well basically, she helped me out a lot with my research into potion-making once, and we've stayed in touch through letters ever since...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so Ying'er is the girl from Liyue that Sucrose mentioned earlier?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We always assumed you were hard at work every time we saw you at the Crafting Bench... So you've just been writing letters to Ying'er the whole time!?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: No! I mean, not ALL the time. I've done some work, too... And anyway, our correspondence covers a lot of serious topics! Like perfumes, potions, alchemy...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Anyway! A few months ago, I made a vow to the heavens that I will be true to myself and never utter an insincere word until the day that I've managed to win Miss Ying'er's heart!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... at Starsnatch Cliff, you were picking Cecilias as a gift for Ying'er?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: That's right! The Cecilia flower is said to represent a once-wayward heart transformed by the power of love. I couldn't think of a better flower to give than that.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: I know full well that Miss Ying'er is far more knowledgeable than I in both the ways of the world and the ways of our craft... But I thought I should make the effort for once, and put myself out there.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Ahem. Which brings me to the subject of the last few days, and the Windblume Festival... I thought it was time for me to invite Miss Ying'er to Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: But yesterday, Albedo told me that Sucrose has been working hard to help another girl achieve her dream...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: And when I went to take a look at our roster, I saw that she'd done my remaining work for me...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: I feel... incredibly guilty.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: I've been spending all of my time in my own fantasy world while everyone else has been bending over backwards to help other people. How could I ever hope to be worthy of Miss Ying'er's love if I'm so selfish?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Oh, Timaeus...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: And that's why I've decided to join you!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: But, then what about Ying'er...?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Yeah, haven't you been planning this for over a month now? You said you were gonna invite her to Mondstadt...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Yes... I did mention in my letters that I'd like her to visit. Which is why I just sent her another gift with my handpicked Windblumes, along with a handwritten letter.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: I explained that a matter of great importance has presented itself to which I must devote my full attention for the time being. As soon as it's resolved, I'll make haste to Liyue to pick her up in person.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: I made sure to package the gift and letter with the greatest care. All I can do now is hope that she'll understand...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: ...Point being, please know that I sincerely want to support you in this endeavor! Plus, I think I'm an honest person... As far as I recall, I don't think I've told a single lie in my life...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, you certainly convinced Paimon with that speech! Don't worry, Timaeus, we won't let your determination go to waste!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: ...Thank you, Timaeus.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Ahh, thank you, everyone! I promise to do everything I can to help!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Okay, so it looks like we've found our "one who would never lie."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! Let's keep it up, on to the other three!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After some discussion, the group decides on a final pick for each part of the prophecy. Everyone gathers in front of the Crafting Bench.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, Paimon will do the honors! *clears throat*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We have with us here the flower, the guide, the legend... and Timaeus.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Huh? Why did you only say Timaeus's name? You should say my name, too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, alright! We also have Klee.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: That's me! Hehehe~

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: With Klee here, this all somehow feels like we're getting ready for a field trip...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: There's nothing wrong with a more relaxed atmosphere, is there?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Albedo, have you figured out your answer?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Of course. We will soon see if my hypothesis has any merit.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Actually... I'm still feeling a little nervous.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Me too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But weren't you all fired up just a moment ago?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Uh, yeah, you're right... Okay, let's do this!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Actually, I'm a little worried too... Deep breaths... deep breaths!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I know what you're feeling... Saying anything becomes so much harder when there are so many people watching...

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Well, does anyone know the exact location of where we're headed? Or should I do a reading on my scryglass?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Hmm, according to the prophecy, once we've figured out the answer, we should test it at the Lantern of Utmost Joy... Wait, but where is this lantern?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, we know something about that!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I've already found out where it is.

response.speaker: Sucrose & Collei
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Sucrose & Collei
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You make up a story about how you discovered the location by divining the wind...

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Wow, that's amazing! You really know how to do everything under the sun...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Then we'll let you lead the way.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Follow me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is it! We're off to find the sacred location of the Lantern of Utmost Joy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How did this little island get up here in the sky? Did somebody make it?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Just to be safe, I've been jotting down our entire route here. This way, no one will get lost!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Good thinking, Collei!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, who would've thought we'd find this kind of table here... Weird, it's almost as if someone was holding a tea party.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I never would've guessed that such a place could exist, right above Mondstadt too...

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Wow, look at the pretty lantern on the table! There's even a chair for each side of the lantern, too!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: There seems to be something on the back of this chair. Let me have a closer look...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: "Take your seat, present your answers, and you shall reach enlightenment."

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, as far as instructions go, I guess that's simple enough...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: So we just need to do as it says, right?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Wait a second.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What is it, Albedo?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We'd better make sure this place is safe before taking our seats. Everyone, please stay clear for a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone vigilantly watches as Albedo conducts a thorough investigation of the space...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, all our questions and doubts aside, the scenery here is pretty amazing! It'd be impossible to feel stressed here.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: How is everything, Albedo?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hmm, everything seems to be fine. I didn't find any traps or suspicious mechanisms.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But, I also couldn't find any overt destructive devices...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean...?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Well, it seems that wrong answers won't have any catastrophic consequences. Looks like we'll have to sit on these chairs and fulfill the prophecy.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Everyone, I would like to suggest that we try some risky answers on our first attempt. Let's reserve our most confident answers for the second round.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds kind of smart... But why?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Ah, I get what he means! If we do as he says, then we may be able to figure out how the puzzle works.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I see! That makes a lot of sense.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mona, is there something wrong? You're not looking too good.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Oh, are you hungry? I brought some snacks...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Thank you for offering, Klee, but that's not quite it!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: While Albedo was checking just now, I gave my scryglass a spin, hoping to find some information...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: But there's a strange aura to this place. It's almost as if someone has been staring at me as soon as we stepped foot in here.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: But if nothing here has actually been physically tampered with, then... No... Could that person be...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Mona just shivered... Did she sense some kind of great power?)

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: What do you mean, Mona? Who could it be?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...Ugh, never mind. It's not like I've got any proof.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Don't leave us on the edge like this, Mona!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'll just do what Albedo said!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes, let's test the hypothesis together, Klee.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Mhm! C'mon, join us, Mona!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Oh... Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Okay... Then I'll answer the first question. If someone were to ask me to find "a flower that is not of this world"...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: You can do it, Sucrose!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Umm...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Then I would fetch a Tetratanic Sweet Flower!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Alright, I'm up next... My part of the prophecy is to find "a guide who will never get lost."

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: (Collei... I hope you found your answer...)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: My answer is... that I will be that guide.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: For a long time, I have been guided by others. It's taken me a while, but I've finally made it to where I am today.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Although I still haven't made a name for myself, and I'm still quite immature, I... I would still like to put my name forward, because I would like to become a guide that can help others.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I want to help others the same way Amber, Master Tighnari, Cyno, and everyone else helped me. Now it's my turn to pass on the gift that I've been given.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Alright, it's up to me to answer the third part. I—I'll submit myself as "one who would never lie."

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Although I've never really had any other virtues or talents, I'm confident that I've always been an honest person.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I—I'd like to thank everyone, too, for giving me this opportunity to validate myself.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: And last but not least, I will answer the final part of the prophecy.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: There's no tale more befitting the title of "a legend that never ends" than our fates as human beings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, the Lantern just lit up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, all four sides of the Lantern are glowing!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh? But...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But all we did was submit a batch of test answers...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Collei, could I ask you to stand up for a second?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, a—alright...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why is it lighting up regardless of who's sitting in the chair? Didn't it say we have to answer all the questions correctly?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's pretty clear now, isn't it? We've just proven that there is no "right answer" for this prophecy.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: No right answer? But how could that be...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Although the instructions had come from an old and enigmatic prophecy, it is in fact nothing like the ancient mechanism that we had all imagined it to be. I believe the lantern only serves as a simple signal...
Ah, and to think, I never expected you to actually find this place...

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: What!? There's someone else here?

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: We meet again, Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey... you're that outlander we met the other day at Good Hunter.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to you that I was able to find this place. Good thing that you were too preoccupied with the prophecy to notice someone tailing you from the shadows.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh, is that so? Then why do I spy yet another person following in your shadow?

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: ...Wait, really!?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: There's no need for pleasantries. You should know I'm here for you.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Is it just because I'm a visitor from abroad?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: I was there when you snuck your way into Marjorie's place.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Heh, so you had your eyes on me even then, huh? That was two whole weeks ago, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: It's hard not to notice you when I'm on duty every day.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Alright, in that case, I'll admit it. I was the person who slipped this prophecy into the storybook.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh? But why? Then... does that mean... this wasn't a real prophecy after all?

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Don't worry. Even though you probably have plenty of reservations about me, you can be sure that the prophecy is genuine.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: In fact, many of you here today may have heard the codename of the one who left the prophecy to me.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: She hailed from an ancient assembly of powerful women, each of whom used a single letter to signify themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Who would've guessed... It seems that power was indeed left behind by the old hag after all...

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Ah, so you're B's student. It's an honor to meet you. I am Scarlett, the successor of J.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Wh—What are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: It's a long story, but I'm not quite sure that I'm the best person to tell it.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Since you've all spent so much time and energy trying to decipher this prophecy, you must also be very interested in the secret behind this lantern, no?

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: The lantern has already been lit. Now then... "Please allow me to disturb your happy peace."
...Huh? Why did this little thing just light up? How strange...

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Hello? On the other side of the lantern... can you hear me over there?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Mom?
Hmm? Oh, I hear many youthful voices...

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Madam, I am Scarlett, the successor of J.
Oh, ahem! Since we've last gathered, J's successor has already become so reckless and bold. Unbelievable...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Wait wait wait, why are you talking just like the old hag!?
Old hag? Who would dare say that... Is that Mona?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Who are you! Who dares imitate my master!?
Ahem... Hmph, and what of imitation and mimicry? It has always been a fool's errand to mimic and learn from humanity...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Aunt Alice. I'm here too.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Moooom! Why are you trying to talk like other people?
Hehehe... so I see everyone's here. Well then, my warmest greetings, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Miss Alice, why would you...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Well, it's been many years since this Lantern last lit up! You can't blame me for thinking that one of the old friends from my youth may have decided to catch up again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, why's she sound so coy all of a sudden...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: And if I recall correctly, we left this lantern in the care of the Anemo Archon, Barbatos... Hmm, you must be commended for uncovering an artifact entrusted to the God of Wind himself.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Tell me, are you sitting around my beloved tea party table?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: It's a reeeeeeeally long table!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Oho, so you are... I suppose this means even the Anemo Archon has granted you entry to this place. Was all of this Scarlett's doing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait wait, Paimon's completely lost now... So what was this "assembly" you were talking about earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Miss Alice, would it be alright to leave the explanation of that to you?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hehe, well, you should be rewarded for making it all the way up here and activating the lantern. Now then, let me tell you a long and ancient story...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, so this is where the legendary mages held their meetings.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: That's right! We often met here to chat and have tea.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Th—Then what about the part saying that if we light the lantern of utmost joy, we'd receive a supreme blessing?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Ah, about that... Ehehe, I never expected anyone other than J to actually read the full contents of that prophecy. It's a little embarrassing...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: The truth is, that prophecy was actually just a letter that we sent to J as a group the day before her wedding.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hmm, so it was indeed written by all of you.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hehe, I must thank you for resisting the urge to immediately reveal the truth to everybody, Albedo. Knowing you, you probably figured out everything the moment you laid eyes on the message.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: No, it took me a little longer than that.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: "A flower that is not of this world"... "A guide who will never get lost"... "One who would never lie"... And "a legend that never ends." These four descriptions signify four individual mages.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: When a member of the organization had to leave the group to spend the rest of her days with her beloved, the other mages would write down this prophecy and send it to her to invite her for a final get-together.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: "A flower that is not of this world" signifies, of course, flowers that do not naturally exist in this world. This is the signature of R, full name Rhinedottir, also known as "Gold."

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: If there's anyone in this world who could create a flower species that does not yet exist, it would be her.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: The "guide who will never get lost" is N, otherwise known as Nicole. You may have not encountered her yet, but she is a truly extraordinary woman who has made this world's direction and order her subject of study.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Some of you may be fortunate enough to have already heard her voice. Like a prophetess, she will only speak to guide people toward the truth when a change has occurred in the world.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: She has a tendency to... suddenly speak in someone's mind without any warning.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(Huh! Could she have been the one who spoke to me while we were investigating {REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}...?)

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: If one day, you would be unfortunate enough to run into a truly dangerous situation, she may use her voice to guide the way forward for you.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Who would have guessed that there are so many mysterious women in this world, and that they would all know each other...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: The "one who would never lie" is... me. I hope no one would take offense — it's just that I, Alice, or "A" for short, have always had a soft spot for those with sincerity and candor.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: As for "a legend that never ends"... You may not know M in person, but you've likely encountered one of her works. Have any of you ever read "The Boar Princess"?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Huh? I'm pretty sure every child in Mondstadt has read that book.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's also one of my favorite stories. M was an exceptional human writer who used her prose to teach me the meaning of grief.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Don't you think such a person would deserve a seat at the mages' table?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's getting more and more lost...

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: It may sound hard to believe, but I can attest to everything that Alice has said. J was also a mortal who aged and passed on, leaving her title to her students and followers.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Alice... You've never acknowledged any of J's successors. It's now been centuries since the first of us took on her mantle. I've always wanted to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Do you also want to become a mage?

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Title aside, I think I'm more interested in the meaning and purpose of the Hexenzirkel.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: I used to think that the Hexenzirkel was a group of women who could control the very fate of this world. But now... I've seen for myself that besides J, many other ordinary people were also among you.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Do you think less of us now?

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: No, not at all. My interest has been piqued, and I'm now even more drawn towards the idea of becoming a mage.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: You're right, I've never acknowledged any of J's successors, but you are different. You are much more fascinating than any of your predecessors.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh, has someone finally piqued Aunt Alice's interest?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Now is not a good time, Scarlett, but as soon as I am able, I will seek you out for a meeting. I want you to tell me all about J's married life back in her hometown.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, the mage who received the prophecy letter from all of you was J? She left the Hexenzirkel after getting married?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Precisely. There was only one way the letter could have been interpreted. She would have known what we meant as soon as she saw the message. We were just asking one thing of her...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: "Please come to see us again. Before you go and settle forever with your happiness, please come share some of it with your best friends and sisters."

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: So, the "supreme blessing" actually meant...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: All journeys are fleeting, and will eventually come to an end. What will give us the most fulfillment and happiness in the end are those who will greet us at our journey's destination.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Dear child, I believe you can also understand what I am talking about. We women will always have many troubles, and encounter pains and frustrations that will keep us up at night.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: But no matter how hard things may become, we will cross mountains and oceans to see our best friends again... Regardless of how many years have passed, or how far the distance may be...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: As long as we can be with our beloved friends, our hearts will be filled with joy. To us mages, that's what being "supremely blessed" is all about.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Uh, I still don't really get it, but I do know that all the mages are Mom's best friends!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hehehe... If you ask how I see it, the Hexenzirkel is just a group of ladies that I spent my youth with.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Anyway, I'll introduce some of the other members to you all later. I still have a few things to attend to, so this will have to do for today.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Bye, Mom! Dodoco says bye too!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Goodbye, darling! And farewell to all of our other friends as well. I'm sure we'll see each other again.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Ah, now that I think of it, isn't it getting close to... that time of year?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Yes, it's Windblume again, Alice.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: It's also a special anniversary date. I'm sure you still remember...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Yes, I do remember now. It was on this day, many, many years ago, that J tied the knot.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Ah, just in time for the festival of love and freedom. Everyone, please enjoy this year's Windblume festival to the fullest.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Aww... I don't see any lanterns here.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Hmm, now that I think about it, the prophecy didn't say anything about what the Lantern of Utmost Joy actually looks like, right? Maybe we've overlooked something?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, are you trying to figure out something else from the paper?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Venti's note here says we should look up and seek the answer from the sky.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's reading too... Huh, it says to look up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... But there's nothing above us! The wind didn't trick us, did it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The slip also says: "Now, you should recite the incantation"...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, take a look at this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Place the squirrel on the back of the pointy-eared cat, and a pious puppy will open the doors to show you the way..." Huh, Paimon read the whole thing out loud, but nothing's happening...

talks.objective: Go to where the Lantern of Utmost Joy is

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Look, look! The wind is blowing!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: What a strong wind current... Let's ride it up and see where it leads us.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Huh? We'll have to fly up there? Uh, can someone carry me with them...?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Here.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Ohh, ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Are you okay, Timaeus? Maybe you'd feel better if you just... you know, let it out...

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I'm fine, I'm fine, I'm just... a little glidersick, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You may want to look into getting your own gliding license when you have the time. It might prove helpful to you.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Ah, okay... sure thing...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: It sounds like you've still got something on your mind... Why don't you tell us, we're all happy to listen!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: *sigh* It's nothing, really, it's just... Well, Alice's story WAS really interesting and romantic, I won't argue about that.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: But still... the whole thing wasn't quite what I was hoping for.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Of course, I didn't actually expect the supreme blessing to be real, but... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ah, don't say that! None of this was your fault, Timaeus. Honestly, it's more on me for having agreed to be the Windblume Festival Special Ambassador. Had I not asked for everyone's help...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: If anything, it should be my fault for finding that prophecy...

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: No no no, I didn't mean to blame the two of you either! I just feel like... this whole adventure didn't really end on a high note, and we also didn't really get anything out of it.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Hmm... But I'd say we still learned something new.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Well, that aside, Timaeus... You still need to go to Liyue to apologize to Ying'er, right? Do you want Collei and I to accompany you?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Oh, Miss Ying'er... Well... I mean, I just really don't want her to get mad at me! Now that I've come back to my senses, I really don't know what I should do...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hey, you three... You may want to look over there.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: M—Miss Ying'er!?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's Miss Ying'er!? I've never met her before...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, that's her! And she actually came all the way to Mondstadt...

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm so sorry, Miss Ying'er... But how did you... I mean...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Hehe, are you so happy just to see me?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I, uh... of course I am! I'm so happy that... I don't, uh... Sorry, I don't know what to say...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: I was ready to give you a harsh scolding, but now that I've seen you like this, I suppose I could let you off the hook this time.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: You said you couldn't come to pick me up because of a very important matter, right? Well then, of course I had to come and find you instead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe... should we go see how they're doing?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I wouldn't. You'll get hit by a forest boar if you interrupt a couple's romantic conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh really? Uh, we'll just leave them alone then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (They look quite happy... Maybe that's what Windblume's all about.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Their adventure has come to an end. Everyone bids farewell, and soon, only a few people are left standing by the crafting bench...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I am so glad to see Timaeus find his happiness...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I have to say, I'm even more envious of you, Sucrose...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: You can be happy just to see others happy, and you gave me so much help without any expectations in return... Even though you said that we're very much alike, I still feel like you have a much bigger heart than I do.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: But if you say that, then I'd say I'm also nowhere near as brave or tenacious as you. I guess we have the same amount of positive qualities... they're just spread over different parts of our personalities.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I've never visited Sumeru, or made many friends from outside of Mondstadt. I'm happy just to have met and become your friend.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Maybe I'll get shy and flustered when I meet other people I don't know in the future... But that's okay, too.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Since we are so alike, you probably get what I'm trying to say. You just need to believe that all of your "issues" aren't really issues at all!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But... Isn't it too late now for me to learn to accept myself?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Uh, well... Hmm, do you know anything about the blooming cycles of Cecilias?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Umm... I may have read about that in a book before.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: That's a topic that my parents used to talk about back when they were still dating. Surprising, right? To think that people would talk about that while on a date.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: My mom brought it up at dinner one time last month. She called my dad the most boring man she knew, and said that he even turned up late to a date once... all with a smile on her face.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: But she also said that learning is just another part of life. It's never too late to start something as long as you recognize that it's something good for you to do.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Why don't you give it a try, Collei?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...Okay! I'll try my best.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They're really having a great conversation... Paimon can't even find a moment to join in.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, isn't it great that they're getting along so well?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ah, I nearly forgot! This is for you.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: This texture... Are these seeds?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yep! I believe I mentioned my Sweet Flower research to you before. These are the seeds of the Sweet Flower cultivars that I have worked on.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: It's nothing too special, but they're the best cultivars that I've made! So... I really hope that you'll like them...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: They're super sweet, and easy to grow and keep!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I'm also submitting them as my Windblumes for this year. I wish that the Anemo Archon could also see how lovely they are...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Thank you! I'll plant them in the Avidya Forest, and take good care of them.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Collei, please take these notes with you.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I've heard that you've been working hard on your studies, so I've prepared some study materials for you at Sucrose's request. Feel free to look through them whenever you can find the time. Mondstadt's doors will always remain open to you.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah... Thank you so much... Really... I...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I don't know what to say. I... I'm just really happy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Sucrose! Now's your chance! Didn't you want to collect a "Breath of Joy"?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ahhh, you're right, I almost forgot! Collei, can you exhale once into this test tube? I will save this breath of joy, and use it in my research.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, really? May I?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Of course!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Huh...? What... what was that?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: It was like a little cloud of happiness, but now it flew away...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Well, luckily there's still some breath left in the test tube... I'll seal it up for now.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I'll keep working on it and let you know as soon as I have any breakthroughs in my research!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yeah, you can write to me! I'll be sure to respond as soon as I receive your letter.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh, it looks like you've found a new pen pal?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Master Tighnari! Cyno!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If your friendship was forged in a test tube, does that make you "test friends forever"?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That's it... I think you've ruined Sumeru's reputation in Mondstadt beyond all hope of repair.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: All that matters is that I've enjoyed Mondstadt immensely. The dragon here possesses a majestic form.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #Ah, that reminds me. {NICKNAME}, this card back is for you.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Cyno wanted you to have one for yourself. If I had to guess, I'd say he probably wants you to use it if you challenge him to a duel.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I'm a master of the game. Do you dare challenge me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can you believe this guy!? Let's knock him off his high horse!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's time to duel!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: W—Wait, I've got something to give you, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, Collei has a gift for us?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Yeah. I... figured I should follow local Mondstadt customs, and prepared a few small things themed after the Windblume Festival.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I made these bookmarks from Sumeru Roses at the hotel... I want to give them to Amber, Master Tighnari, and Cyno.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: During Windblume, Mondstadters offer flowers to the people most important to them... you three are family to me.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: But Tighnari said that we're not anything like an academic family. He wouldn't write joint papers with us...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Well, in this case, we can consider ourselves as regular siblings, and that should be just fine.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Hehe, I agree!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: #Oh, and here are some Padisarah seeds as well... These are for {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and everyone else from Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Are these really for us?

choices.text: Thank you. We really appreciate it.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: So, are these your chosen Windblumes?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Mhm, one of them! Both Padisarahs and Sumeru Roses are my Windblumes.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Although they're not native to Mondstadt, they are the flowers that can best express my feelings.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I want to give them to the people I feel thankful for, to those who... I wish to accompany as we greet more seasons and future Windblumes together.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: The real blessing in life is when you are surrounded by people who you'd miss day and night, and who you'd want to see even if that meant crossing mountains and oceans to do so.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Hehe! I'm so happy to hear you say that.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Sucrose, do you see that cloud over there?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Doesn't it look... just like your test tube?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Alice's voice fades, and the lantern grows dim. It is once again just a regular piece of decor.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: \nFor a moment, everyone looks lost in thought, but soon, chatter begins to fill the space again. Before long, everyone spreads their gliders to return to Mondstadt.
